newsitem.title: UK: Bond markets stymied in latest week -Salomon data.
newsitem.headline: Bond markets stymied in latest week -Salomon data.

text.p: Major government bond markets spent a frustrating week getting nowhere, latest data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday. Four of the 16 markets covered in the index finished the week ended Thursday at or near where they started and the global index as a whole was 0.01 percent down.

U.S. Treasuries were exactly unchanged in local currency terms, as where Danish bonds. Austrian bonds showed a tiny 0.01 percent return, while Belgian bonds managed 0.02 percent. French OATs, turning in a 0.26 percent return in French francs, were the top performers.
Japanese government bonds (JGBs), showing a loss of the exact same amount in yen terms, were worst.
The latest week is in contrast to most periods of market action where bonds often show returns or losses of one percent or more.
But in dollar terms, there was a clearer trend as the U.S. currency registered gains against most markets, which thus showed losses for dollar-based investors.
Of the bond markets listed 12 showed losses in dollar terms.
Swiss bonds, the second highest returner in local currency terms with a 0.24 percent gain, was the worst performing in dollars with a 1.74 percent loss.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest. --International bonds unit +44 171 542 6784
